title: Korean Dakdoritang
summary: Tender chicken and potatoes simmered in a bold, spicy-sweet gochugaru broth with garlic and spring onions.

stages.title: Prepare chicken and sauce
steps: Pat chicken dry and trim excess fat; keep pieces similar in size for even cooking.
Mix soy sauce, gochugaru, gochujang, sugar and garlic with 3 tbsp water.

stages.title: Simmer chicken
steps: Place chicken, onion and 500 ml water in a wide pot; bring to a simmer and skim any foam.
Stir in sauce and simmer partially covered for 15 minutes before adding potatoes and carrot.

stages.title: Reduce and serve
steps: Continue simmering 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches 74°C at its thickest point.
Uncover for the last few minutes to concentrate the broth, then scatter spring onions over the top.

tips: Bone-in chicken gives the broth more body; check doneness with a thermometer.
variations: Use less gochugaru for a milder stew.
Add mushrooms in the last 10 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Indian Vegetable Pulao
summary: Fluffy basmati rice scented with whole spices, peas and vegetables, finished with fresh coriander and lemon.

stages.title: Rinse and soak rice
steps: Rinse basmati under cool water until it runs mostly clear to remove surface starch.
Soak 10 minutes while preparing vegetables, then drain thoroughly.

stages.title: Toast aromatics
steps: Heat ghee in a lidded saucepan; fry cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaf for 30 seconds.
Add onion and cook until lightly golden, then stir in carrot and drained rice for 1 minute.

stages.title: Steam the rice
steps: Add water, peas and salt; bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Turn off heat and rest covered for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork and add lemon juice.

tips: Keep the lid closed during steaming so the rice cooks evenly.
variations: Use cauliflower florets instead of peas.
storage: Cool rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; keep up to 1 day and reheat steaming hot once.

title: Indian Paneer Bhurji
summary: Crumbled paneer scrambled with tomatoes, green chilli, ginger and warming spices for a quick, satisfying skillet meal.

stages.title: Cook aromatics
steps: Heat oil in a skillet and sauté onion over medium heat until lightly golden.
Add ginger and chilli and cook 1 minute, stirring to prevent sticking.

stages.title: Reduce tomatoes
steps: Add tomatoes, turmeric, cumin and salt; cook until tomatoes collapse and most liquid evaporates.
Stir in garam masala just before adding paneer.

stages.title: Fold in paneer
steps: Add crumbled paneer and gently fold through the spiced tomato mixture for 2–3 minutes until heated through.
Finish with coriander and serve with toast or roti.

tips: Do not cook paneer too long or it can turn chewy.
variations: Use firm tofu for a dairy-free alternative.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat until piping hot.

title: Italian Arancini al Ragù
summary: Golden crumbed rice balls with a crisp shell, creamy saffron rice and a savoury beef ragù centre.
ingredients: 150 g beef ragù, thick (leftover or from a jar)

stages.title: Cook and chill rice
steps: Bring stock and saffron to a simmer; add rice and cook, stirring often, until tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in butter and Parmesan, spread on a tray and cool completely before shaping.

stages.title: Fill and crumb
steps: With damp hands flatten a handful of cold rice, add a teaspoon of thick ragù and a cube of mozzarella.
Enclose filling completely and form a compact ball; repeat, then coat each in flour, egg and breadcrumbs.

stages.title: Fry and drain
steps: Heat oil in a deep heavy pot to 170–175°C, keeping the pot less than half full.
Fry balls in small batches for 4–6 minutes until deep golden and heated through; drain on a rack and rest briefly before serving.

tips: Cold, fairly dry rice is much easier to shape than warm, loose risotto.
variations: Use peas and mozzarella instead of ragù.
Bake brushed with oil at 200°C until crisp for a lighter finish.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate up to 2 days; reheat thoroughly until hot in the centre.

title: Greek Spanakorizo
summary: Tender rice simmered with spinach, dill and spring onions, finished with lemon and extra virgin olive oil.

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Heat olive oil in a deep pan and soften onion for 5–6 minutes.
Add spring onions and cook another minute before stirring in rice.

stages.title: Wilt spinach and simmer
steps: Add spinach in handfuls, stirring until wilted; add stock and a pinch of salt.
Cover and simmer gently for 18–20 minutes until rice is tender, adding a little hot water if needed.

stages.title: Finish with lemon
steps: Remove from heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fold in chopped dill, lemon juice and zest; drizzle with olive oil and season to taste.

tips: Add lemon at the end to keep its flavour fresh and bright.
variations: Use frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry.
storage: Cool rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; keep up to 1 day and reheat thoroughly once.

title: Georgian Chakhokhbili
summary: Chicken braised with juicy tomatoes, onions and fragrant coriander in a bright, comforting Georgian stew.

stages.title: Sear chicken
steps: Pat chicken dry, season and brown in oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side.
Transfer to a plate; it will finish cooking in the sauce.

stages.title: Cook vegetables
steps: Soften onions and sliced pepper in the same pan for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ground coriander, stirring until fragrant.

stages.title: Braise and finish
steps: Add tomatoes and chicken with accumulated juices; cover and simmer gently for 18–20 minutes until chicken reaches 74°C.
Scatter coriander leaves over the stew and serve with bread.

tips: Use thigh meat to keep the chicken juicy during braising.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Peruvian Papa a la Huancaina
summary: Tender potato slices covered in a silky, mildly spicy cheese and yellow chilli sauce with olives and egg.

stages.title: Cook potatoes
steps: Boil whole potatoes in salted water until a knife slips in easily, about 18–20 minutes.
Drain, cool slightly, peel if desired and cut into thick slices.

stages.title: Blend sauce
steps: Blend feta, evaporated milk, aji amarillo, crackers and oil until smooth.
Add water by the tablespoon if too thick; taste before salting.

stages.title: Plate and serve
steps: Arrange lettuce and potato slices on a platter.
Spoon sauce generously over potatoes and garnish with quartered eggs and olives.

tips: Start with less chilli paste and adjust to your preferred heat.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Indonesian Sayur Lodeh
summary: Vegetables simmered in gently spiced coconut broth with lemongrass, galangal and tender green beans.

stages.title: Prepare paste
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger and turmeric with a splash of water to a coarse paste.
Bruise lemongrass with the back of a knife to release aroma.

stages.title: Cook aromatics
steps: Fry spice paste in oil for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add lemongrass and stir for another minute.

stages.title: Simmer vegetables
steps: Pour in water and coconut milk, then add carrot and aubergine; simmer gently 10 minutes.
Add beans and cabbage and cook until just tender, keeping the broth below a hard boil.

tips: Gentle heat helps prevent the coconut broth from splitting.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Sri Lankan Pol Sambol
summary: Fresh grated coconut tossed with chilli, lime and red onion for a punchy, aromatic accompaniment.

stages.title: Prepare aromatics
steps: Finely mince red onion and chilli, removing seeds if you prefer less heat.
Combine with salt and chilli flakes in a mortar or sturdy bowl.

stages.title: Mix sambol
steps: Lightly pound the onion mixture to release its juices.
Add coconut and lime juice and mix thoroughly until evenly seasoned.

stages.title: Adjust and serve
steps: Taste for salt, heat and acidity, adding extra lime if needed.
Serve immediately alongside rice, curry or hoppers.

tips: Fresh coconut gives the best texture; thaw frozen grated coconut fully before using.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Mexican Rajas con Crema
summary: Strips of roasted poblano pepper and sweet onion coated in a silky, lightly tangy cream sauce.

stages.title: Roast peppers
steps: Char poblano peppers under a hot grill, turning until skins blister.
Cover 10 minutes, then peel, deseed and slice into strips.

stages.title: Cook onion
steps: Heat oil and soften onion over medium heat until translucent and lightly golden.
Add sliced peppers and corn, stirring until warmed through.

stages.title: Add cream
steps: Lower heat and stir in sour cream with 2 tbsp water; warm gently without boiling.
Add cheese and stir until just melted, then season and serve with tortillas.

tips: Keep heat low after adding cream to prevent separation.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Italian Bagna Cauda
summary: A warm Piedmontese dip of gently melted anchovies and garlic in olive oil, served with crisp vegetables.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Wash and cut carrots, celery, capsicum and fennel into long dipping sticks.
Arrange vegetables on a platter and keep chilled until serving.

stages.title: Soften garlic
steps: Heat olive oil and butter in a small saucepan over very low heat.
Add sliced garlic and cook gently for 10–12 minutes until completely soft without browning.

stages.title: Melt anchovies
steps: Add anchovies and stir until they dissolve into the warm oil.
Serve the dip warm in a heatproof bowl with raw vegetables.

tips: Never fry the garlic hard; gentle cooking gives a sweet, mellow sauce.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Turkish Ezogelin Soup
summary: Red lentils, bulgur and mint simmered with tomato and pepper paste into a hearty, tangy Turkish soup.

stages.title: Soften onion
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan and cook diced onion until soft and translucent.
Stir in tomato and pepper pastes and cook 1 minute to deepen flavour.

stages.title: Simmer grains
steps: Add rinsed lentils, bulgur and stock; bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils break down and bulgur softens.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Stir in dried mint and paprika, thinning with hot water if needed.
Season with salt and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

tips: Stir near the end as lentils and bulgur can stick when thickened.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Ethiopian Shiro Wat
summary: Silky chickpea flour stew simmered with berbere, onion and garlic until thick and aromatic.

stages.title: Cook onion
steps: Soften onion in oil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until sweet.
Add garlic, berbere and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.

stages.title: Whisk flour
steps: Whisk chickpea flour into 250 ml cold water until completely smooth.
Slowly pour into the pan while stirring to prevent lumps.

stages.title: Simmer
steps: Add remaining water gradually and simmer over low heat 15–20 minutes until thick and silky.
Season with salt and serve with injera or flatbread.

tips: Whisk chickpea flour with cold water first to prevent lumps.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Filipino Ginataang Kalabasa
summary: Tender pumpkin and green beans in a savoury coconut sauce scented with garlic and ginger.

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Cook onion in oil until translucent, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in fish sauce and 100 ml water.

stages.title: Cook pumpkin
steps: Add pumpkin and simmer covered for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Pour in coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer.

stages.title: Finish beans
steps: Add green beans and cook 5–8 minutes until just tender.
Season to taste and serve with rice.

tips: Keep coconut milk at a gentle simmer to prevent splitting.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Greek Kolokithokeftedes
summary: Crisp courgette and feta fritters flecked with mint and dill, served with cool yoghurt.

stages.title: Drain courgettes
steps: Grate courgettes, sprinkle with salt and rest 10 minutes.
Squeeze firmly in a clean towel to remove as much water as possible.

stages.title: Mix fritters
steps: Combine courgettes with crumbled feta, eggs, flour, chopped herbs and spring onions.
Stir just until mixture holds together.

stages.title: Pan-fry
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and spoon small patties into pan.
Cook 3–4 minutes each side until golden and cooked through; drain on a rack.

tips: Removing courgette moisture is essential for crisp fritters.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Mexican Enfrijoladas
summary: Warm corn tortillas folded through a smoky black bean sauce and topped with cheese and onion.

stages.title: Blend bean sauce
steps: Blend beans with stock, garlic, half the onion and chipotle until smooth.
Add more stock if needed for a pourable sauce.

stages.title: Simmer sauce
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil and simmer blended beans for 8–10 minutes until silky.
Season to taste and keep warm over low heat.

stages.title: Fill tortillas
steps: Warm tortillas in a lightly oiled pan until flexible.
Dip each into bean sauce, fold onto plates and top with crumbled cheese, onion and coriander.

tips: Warm tortillas first so they fold without cracking.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Japanese Kabocha Nimono
summary: Sweet Japanese pumpkin simmered in a delicate dashi, soy and mirin broth until tender and glossy.

stages.title: Cut pumpkin
steps: Remove seeds and cut kabocha into even chunks, leaving some skin attached.
Place pieces skin-side down in a snug saucepan.

stages.title: Mix broth
steps: Combine dashi, soy, mirin and sugar, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Pour over pumpkin so pieces are partly submerged.

stages.title: Gentle simmer
steps: Cover with a parchment lid or loose lid and simmer gently 15–20 minutes until a skewer slides in easily.
Rest in the broth for 5 minutes before serving.

tips: Avoid stirring aggressively; cooked kabocha breaks apart easily.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Algerian Hmiss
summary: Smoky roasted peppers and tomatoes mashed with garlic, olive oil and a pinch of cumin.

stages.title: Char vegetables
steps: Grill whole capsicums and tomatoes, turning until skins blister and flesh softens.
Cover briefly, then peel peppers, remove seeds and chop vegetables.

stages.title: Cook garlic
steps: Warm olive oil in a pan and gently cook minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Add cumin and stir until fragrant without browning.

stages.title: Reduce and serve
steps: Add chopped peppers and tomatoes and cook until excess moisture evaporates.
Mash coarsely, season with salt and lemon, and serve with bread.

tips: Cook away excess liquid for a thick, scoopable dip.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: French Far Breton
summary: A tender baked Breton custard studded with soft prunes and lightly scented with vanilla.

stages.title: Prepare pan
steps: Heat oven to 180°C and butter a 24 cm baking dish.
Scatter prunes evenly over the bottom.

stages.title: Mix batter
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar, then add flour until smooth.
Gradually whisk in milk and vanilla to form a thin custard batter.

stages.title: Bake and cool
steps: Pour batter over prunes and bake 40–45 minutes until puffed and golden with a slight wobble.
Cool until set before slicing.

tips: Rest after baking so the custard firms up cleanly.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.

title: Korean Dubu Jorim
summary: Pan-seared tofu braised in a spicy soy-garlic glaze with spring onions and sesame oil.

stages.title: Prepare tofu
steps: Drain tofu, pat dry and slice into thick rectangles.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.

stages.title: Sear
steps: Cook tofu 3–4 minutes per side until golden and lightly crisp.
Whisk soy, gochugaru, garlic, sugar and water together.

stages.title: Braise
steps: Pour sauce around tofu and simmer 5–7 minutes until slightly reduced.
Spoon glaze over tofu and finish with spring onions and sesame oil.

tips: Dry tofu thoroughly so it browns rather than steams.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly if served hot.
